# ServOS iOS shells (WKWebView) — POS + KDS

iPad-first WebView wrappers around the PROD web app, mirroring the Android wrapper in `android/`.

**One project, one source tree, multiple app targets.** Every app compiles the SAME Swift files in `ServOSPOS/`; anything app-specific comes from that target's Info.plist (generated by XcodeGen from its `info.properties` stanza in `project.yml`).

| Target | Bundle id | URL | Camera |
|---|---|---|---|
| ServOS POS | `co.posup.rpos.pos` | `https://possystem-liard.vercel.app/?mode=pos` | yes (QR scanning) |
| ServOS KDS | `co.posup.rpos.kds` | `https://possystem-liard.vercel.app/?mode=kds` | no |

- **No .xcodeproj in git.** `xcodegen generate` builds it from `project.yml` (XcodeGen 2.46.0 installed).
- **No hardware bridges in v1.** `window.RposPrinter` is left undefined on purpose, so printing falls back to the Supabase `print_jobs` queue and the LAN print agent. The shell injects `window.RposIOS = { platform: 'ios', version: '<marketing version>' }` so the web app can detect it.

## Per-app Info.plist keys (the contract)

`ServOSPOS/Config.swift` reads these at runtime; the Swift sources contain NO per-app values.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `RPOSAppURL` | String, **required** | The web app URL this shell hosts and retries. Missing/invalid = deliberate `fatalError` at launch. |
| `RPOSAllowsCamera` | Bool, optional | `true`: the WKWebView grants getUserMedia CAMERA requests from our origin (the target must ALSO declare `NSCameraUsageDescription`). Absent or `false`: camera denied and no permission string ships (KDS). Microphone is always denied for every target. |

Everything shared (internal host allowlist, 5 s retry loop, keep-awake, zoom/bounce/callout lockdown, Safari handoff for external links) stays as code in `ServOSPOS/`. `ReconnectingView` names the app from `CFBundleDisplayName`.

## Asset catalogs (per target)

- `ServOSPOS/Assets.xcassets` — POS `AppIcon` + `LaunchBackground` colorset (Ink `#0F1211`).
- `ServOSKDS/Assets.xcassets` — KDS `AppIcon` + its own copy of `LaunchBackground`.

The KDS icon is a placeholder derived from the POS master with Pillow: full-bleed the green `#15C26A`, cover the POS wordmark, set "KDS" in Helvetica Neue Condensed Black at the same cap height and position, 1024 square RGB with no alpha. Replace with a real brand export before App Store submission.

## Add a new app target (recipe)

1. In `project.yml`, copy the whole `ServOS KDS:` target stanza AND its scheme stanza. Rename both.
2. Change `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` (e.g. `co.posup.rpos.tables`), `PRODUCT_NAME`, `CFBundleDisplayName`, and `info.path` (e.g. `ServOSTables/Info.plist`).
3. Set `RPOSAppURL` to the new surface URL, and `RPOSAllowsCamera` (+ `NSCameraUsageDescription` only if true).
4. Create `ServOSTables/Assets.xcassets` with an `AppIcon.appiconset` (single 1024 universal PNG, RGB, no alpha) and a `LaunchBackground.colorset` (copy from `ServOSKDS/Assets.xcassets`). Point the new target's second `sources` path at it.
5. `xcodegen generate`, then register the new bundle id in the developer portal (or let Xcode automatic signing do it on first archive) and create the App Store Connect app record.
6. Archive: `xcodebuild archive -project "ServOS POS.xcodeproj" -scheme "<name>" -destination "generic/platform=iOS" -archivePath build/<name>.xcarchive -allowProvisioningUpdates`.

No Swift changes needed. Do not add per-app constants to `Config.swift`; add a plist key instead.

## From zero to TestFlight (owner steps)

1. **Install Xcode** from the Mac App Store (large download, let it finish fully).
2. **Point the tools at it**, in Terminal:
   `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app && sudo xcodebuild -license accept`
3. **Add your Apple ID**: Xcode -> Settings -> Accounts -> + -> your Apple Developer Apple ID.
4. **Generate and open the project**:
   `cd ios && xcodegen generate && open "ServOS POS.xcodeproj"`
5. **Team is pinned**: `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: LYQ8K25MGZ` is already in `project.yml` for every target; signing stays Automatic. A new bundle id registers itself on first automatic signing (or register it at developer.apple.com like POS).
6. **Create the app record**: appstoreconnect.apple.com -> Apps -> + -> New App -> platform iOS, the target's display name, its bundle id.
7. **Archive and upload**: pick the scheme (ServOS POS or ServOS KDS), Product -> Archive -> Distribute App -> TestFlight & App Store -> Upload. CLI archiving with `-allowProvisioningUpdates` also works (proven for POS).
8. **Add testers**: App Store Connect -> your app -> TestFlight -> Internal Testing -> add internal testers.

## Before App Store submission

- **KDS app icon** is a derived placeholder. Export the real KDS mark from the Brand Guidelines before public release.
- **Version bumps**: `MARKETING_VERSION` / `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` live per target in `project.yml` (POS currently 1.0.0 build 3, KDS 1.0.0 build 1). Bump there, regenerate, archive.

## Later automation

- Claude can archive and upload from the CLI once you hand over an **App Store Connect API key**: appstoreconnect.apple.com -> Users and Access -> Integrations -> App Store Connect API -> Team Keys -> Generate (role App Manager). Hand it over the same way as the Supabase PAT.
- `exportOptions.plist` is already set up for that (app-store-connect method, automatic signing).

## Legacy folder

- **`RestaurantOS/`** is the previous hand-assembled UIKit scaffold (bundle id `co.posup.rpos.ios`). It is NOT part of this build; XcodeGen only compiles `ServOSPOS/`. Its `Printer/PrinterBridge.swift` (WKScriptMessageHandler printer bridge) is a useful starting point if a native `RposPrinter` bridge is wanted in v2.

## What the shells do

- **Never sleep**: `isIdleTimerDisabled` on, re-asserted whenever the app becomes active.
- **Never white-screen**: any load failure shows a native Reconnecting view and retries the same URL every 5 seconds until it loads. A killed web process reloads itself.
- **Stay put**: our host and `*.supabase.co` (plus localhost) load in the WebView; everything else opens in Safari.
- **POS-friendly WebView**: no pinch zoom, no scroll bounce, no long-press callouts, inline media with no tap (order chime works). Camera granted to our origin only where `RPOSAllowsCamera` is true (POS); microphone always denied.
- **Orientation**: iPad all orientations, iPhone portrait only (runs on iPhone so TestFlight review cannot crash it). Identical for every target.
